recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-31612 unless a future redesign changes the module diagram level labels or grouping.
issue_request: FHIR-31612 was Published/Persuasive for the FHIR-core Modules page. It asked to clarify text that described Infrastructure as the bottom rung/row, Content as the middle/top row, and Reasoning as the top rung because that contradicted the diagram, and suggested describing the groups by Level 1 through Level 5 and module names.
initial_application: No historical source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-31612 was found. The same source problem was later corrected by commit dfb07285cbc2261914990d8de6a9ac750a96d594 for FHIR-33977, which changed source/modules.html from the old bottom/middle/top rung wording to Infrastructure (Level 1 and Level 2), Content (Level 3 and Level 4), and Reasoning (Level 5).
additional_context: FHIR-31576 raised the same diagram/text mismatch earlier and asked to remove the confusing group text. FHIR-33977 later resolved the same change family with the explicit level-label wording that is now present and already has reconciliation commit 4492cdaf3f3b7a506e9c4ae19076d1da3601cb36 on the combined branch. source/hierarchy.xml lists modules.html as the Getting Started page, and source/modules.html includes source/modules-fragment.html, whose adjacent diagram labels Levels 1 through 5 and names the corresponding modules. FHIR-I Confluence minutes record the FHIR-31612 vote, and bounded Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. source/modules.html currently contains the accepted level-label bullets and no longer contains the misleading rung/row descriptions; adding module-name prose would duplicate the adjacent diagram rather than change implementer understanding.
